status_summary: Executive Order 14187 (signed 2025-01-28) directed HHS action on pediatric gender transition care. HHS rescinded the May 2021 Section 1557 and Title IX notice on 2025-05-14 and published a review of pediatric gender dysphoria evidence (preliminary 2025-05-01, final 2025-11-19). On 2025-10-22 a federal court in Mississippi (Tennessee v. Kennedy) vacated the gender identity provisions of the 2024 Section 1557 rule, and on 2026-06-02 HHS published a notice stating that OCR and CMS will not investigate or enforce them while the vacatur stands. A CMS final rule published 2026-08-13 (CMS-2451-F) took effect on 2026-10-13: it requires state Medicaid plans to bar payment for these procedures for people under 18 (CHIP under 19) and bars federal funds, with up to six months of continued federal match for hormone therapy already under way (not for puberty blockers or surgery). A coalition the Massachusetts Attorney General describes as 22 states (21 attorneys general and one governor) sued in the District of Massachusetts on 2026-09-02, asking the court to declare the rule unlawful; no order blocking or delaying the rule was found as of 2026-10-14. Four New Hampshire families filed a separate suit in the District of New Hampshire on 2026-10-01 seeking to stop enforcement, and no order in it was found as of 2026-10-14. A proposed hospital condition of participation (2025-12-19) had not been finalized, and a proposed rule restoring the 2020 Section 1557 regulation was not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14187 on protecting children from chemical and surgical procedures is signed (published 2025-02-03); Section 5 directs HHS to take actions that may include Medicare and Medicaid conditions of participation.
HHS publishes a notice rescinding four informal guidance documents, including the May 2021 notification of interpretation and enforcement of Section 1557 and Title IX.
CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability rule is published; its abstract says it bars coverage of certain sex-trait modification procedures as an essential health benefit.

S.D. Miss. in Tennessee v. Kennedy vacates the 2024 Section 1557 rule's provisions that extend Title IX's sex discrimination definition to gender identity and enters a declaratory judgment (as later described by HHS).

CMS proposes two rules: a Medicaid and CHIP funding prohibition for these procedures for minors, and a hospital condition of participation barring them for children under 18 (comments on the latter closed 2026-02-17).
HHS publishes a notice of vacatur stating OCR and CMS cannot and will not investigate or enforce the vacated gender identity provisions; other provisions of the 2024 rule remain in force.
CMS publishes the final rule barring Medicaid and CHIP payment for these procedures for minors and barring federal funds for them.

A multistate coalition co-led by the Massachusetts Attorney General (described as 22 states; participants include the District of Columbia and Pennsylvania's governor) sued in the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts to challenge the CMS Medicaid and CHIP rule, which is scheduled to take effect 2026-10-13; the sources read do not state whether the plaintiffs seek to block it before that date.

Four New Hampshire families sue HHS and CMS in the District of New Hampshire (Goe v. HHS; No. 1:26-cv-00803 as listed by plaintiffs' counsel), arguing the Medicaid funding rule conflicts with Medicaid law and exceeds federal authority and asking the court to stop its enforcement; NHPR reported the suit on 2026-10-02 with no hearing or order.
